subject: HaloHealth RAG evaluation: model shortlist, benchmarks and retrieval knobs
summary: Post-demo recap with model recommendations, initial benchmark links, proposed retrieval/reranker config, and two concrete asks: run 1k-shot probe against the shortlisted 1.2B and 7B variants; provide latency/cost tradeoffs for dedicated vs hosted routing.
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@halohealth.ai>, Priya Desai <priya@halohealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + next asks from today's RAG walk-through

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Short recap and concrete next steps so we stay aligned: 

1) What we observed (high level)
- Your team has a mixed knowledge base: patient-facing FAQs (short), clinician protocols (long, structured), and some PDF-scanned lab reports (high OCR noise).
- During the demo the model hallucinated on very recent protocol updates ~2% of probe queries; retrieval coverage looked fine but reranker didn't surface the latest docs.

2) Our recommended direction for the pilot
- Model shortlist: try a quantized 1.2B variant for latency-sensitive endpoints (chat assistant) and a 7B variant for higher-quality summarization/QA paths.
- Retriever config: dense-sparse hybrid with a 512-token passage stride for long protocols + prefix filters for doc-type.
- Reranker: lightweight cross-encoder (distilBERT-based) for final scoring; fall back to lexical score when latency spikes.

3) Deliverables we will provide by EOD Monday
- Benchmark data export (sample responses + token counts) — attached (halo_benchmarks_q2.csv).
- Prompt set (50 probes across priority intents) — attached (prompt_set_v1.txt).
- Initial retriever config (suggested knobs and TTL) — attached (retriever-config.yaml).

4) Asks for your team
- Can you share a short list (5) of the most critical protocols to include in the first pilot?
- Approve an overnight job to run 1k probe queries against both model variants next week so we can quantify regressions and latency.

Next meeting suggestion: 30m on Wed to review probe results and pick the model variant to seed the pilot. Does 10:30–11:00 PT work for you?

Thanks —
Aditya Rao

Subject: RE: Quick recap + next asks from today's RAG walk-through

Adding a few technical notes to the recap and a recommended test matrix for the 1k probes: 

Test matrix (1k probes split)
- 300 short intent QA (FAQ style) — expect high recall, check for hallucination rate.
- 400 long-context extraction (protocol steps) — look at span accuracy and grounding score.
- 200 ambiguity disambiguation (similar docs) — measure reranker precision@1.
- 100 OCR-noise robustness (lab reports) — measure truncated retrieval rate and hallucination.

Model/eval recommendations
- Candidate models: rdw-1.2B-q4 (low latency), rdw-7B-q4 (better understanding), and a baseline open Llama-7B for comparison. We'll provide token-level cost and median p95 latency across the probes.
- Reranker choice: start with a distilled cross-encoder we maintain (fast re-ranking, ~10–20ms per pair on our dedicated pool). If we see recall drops in ambiguity tests, we'll tighten passage windowing before switching to a heavier cross-encoder.

Metrics to surface in the report
- Grounding precision (percentage of answers with at least one supporting doc link)
- Reranker precision@1 and recall@k
- Span F1 for extraction tasks
- Hallucination flag rate (model-produced assertions not found in retrieved docs)
- Cost per 1k probes (tokens + reranker ops) and p95 latency

Operational note
- For the pilot, we recommend instrumenting the prefix/KV cache for common patient-intent prefixes — that alone reduced p95 for similar customers by ~30% in our tests.

I'll stand up the probe harness once Aditya confirms the list of protocols and gives the go-ahead for the runs.

—Marissa
Technical Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
